So a state of the game discussion needs to happen.  We currently have 5 DMs who are writing plot content for s4.  Rob is only doing the crafting system.  We had discussed turning the City into superhero lvl 20 chadding.  But with another borough without DMs, this raises some issues.  Currently, Radar, JJ, Mariam, DMD, and Heki are the ones doing all the plot writing.  Its unsure if the 6 of us could reliably run content for all 5 boroughs, even if we could write it (for instance, although I’m available most days, due to working two jobs, I have to sleep at nights when possible and am not generally available for the evening events, but Crane has assured he is going to help run content, he just hasn't been available to help write).  With only a couple months left to get everything written, finalized, and the server setup, a discussion now of what to do needs to happen.  Radar doesn’t want to spread any of us thinner than we already are (though we might have to depending).  So a few ideas he suggested are:

we could trying talking to a couple mods we know are DMs normally for smaller groups, and ask them if they could step in as DMs.  This might get us a couple more people that could write and run, but we would likely lose some time trying to read them in on everything.

We could write all content in a way that we could have mods help run it or run it with minimal work on our part as the server is running.  This would take a lot more effort now, and we would all have to band together to give the wastes content.

We could move to 3 weeks, possibly with more roleplay intensive weeks (ones without any scheduled events) between.  Those three weeks would be the 3 boroughs we currently have, at one a week, with the other areas that players could interact with, but nothing would be scheduled there.

We could put it off a year, giving us plenty of time to work everything out without having to press or rush for anything, but that might also kill the game and any momentum it has.

These were some of the ideas Radar and I had, but there are likely more.  We could do one or multiple of these.  If you have any ideas, please mention them.
Agreed. But I'd really like to hear from some of the other voices involved before we start making decisions about anything.

Don't put it off, we can do it! I'll be much freer soon with more time to sit down and crank out content. If yall think we need to pull in mods we can do that. I don't think it'd take that long to fill everyone in and am totally willing to help with that. Let's set up a meeting time regardless to talk. I'm free Sunday? Possibly tomorrow night as well.

Very interesting ideas. I personally don’t think we should push it back a year. I think we’d be able to make it.

Also if there are too many burrows, we could keep it at 3, then just spend all 5 weeks in those burrows. That way we don’t have to worry about creating any more areas, and we are able to keep the game up for the length of time that was wanted
depending on work I might be able to make meetings, but regardless, radar knows where I stand.  I agree putting it off a year is bad, but I wanted to suggest every option I could

I'm still a bit torn. 3 weeks 3 boroughs( I think thats still 7 adventures per pair of writers) or 5 weeks 3 boroughs (which adds another 14 days for the 6 of us to divide up)? 6 dms would bring us back to the 2 per borough per week format that made 5 weeks a logical choice. Extending to 5 weeks with three boroughs means each pairing is responsible a bit more work.
Im ok with it either way.

I just want you to make sure you understand that its about 1/3rd more work, and this hopefully the last time we are going to be having the opportunity to make choices. If you are in for 5 weeks I am in.
I have some other weird ides we can use for co-dm'd events and maybe some more things where we include voice actors
Either way
I can meet up any time to tall with you all. Sunday sounds good to me

This is bumping up against my autism. I am not being sarcastic, or trying to be argumentative. I am only trying to understand this in my neuroatypical way.
So, thats an editorial process. Like how do we know how to pick what rules we should poll about?
If this were a 6 person table, obviously dividing it into ranged and melee for every combat would be a pretty rough sacrifice for boss fights

the polling would be best for rules we can't find an agreement on(currently the death save rolling). but i would say mostly polls would suit rulings that affect  player agency so that we can get a beat on how people will feel about it.
and not that we're really arguing about this we're just in a mid-point where it has pros and cons on either way we do it.

So, agency means actions that a player can take to affect their ability to effect the rp world that their character exists in.

so with rule philosophy taken care of, i think players rolling is the best way to go because we do have a semi-large playerbase with anxiety. so simply because we can't guarantee how people would react not knowing what happens behind the curtain we should keep it to the channel and dying role. @here Heki reached out asking if I could make some elemental guns. So before I release them on the ToA server I wanted some input/notes. With that here is "The Gun Show: The General and The Artificer"

**Blazing Bess**
Firearm, two-handed

When tasked by general to design a new firearm, the artificer took his meaning all too literally and thus the Blazing Bess was born. A canister of alchemist’s fire has been retrofitted to the barrel of the gun and set up to shoot more “hot” than lead. The canister has 6 charges and requires help from an artificer to refuel over a short rest. Above the trigger there is a switch that can alternate the firing modes, Heat Wave and Scorcher. Changing the mode requires bonus action.

As an action you can spend one of the charges in the following ways.

Heat Wave: A short range blast of flames sears nearby enemies. Each creature in a 15-foot cone must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 2d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. 

Scorcher: A long blast of flames shoot out 30 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 2d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

**Banshee’s Wail**
Firearm (Musket)

Again the general approached the artificer, demanding a rifle that could strike fear into an enemy whilst they stayed safely in the shadows. Enlisting the help of a Gnermish Gnecromancer, the artificer crafted a most frightening firearm. With a long black finished barrel and silver banding adorned each adorned with protective runes, the Banshee’s Wail was a sight to behold and a terror to hear. 

This musket has an increased short and long range of 300/900, respectively. When you fire the gun an anguished wailing fills the air, each creature in a 15-foot-radius centered on the target creature must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or drop whatever they are holding and become frightened for 1 minute. If a creature succeeds on the saving throw they are immune to the affect for 24 hours.

If you hit a target affected by the frightened condition with Banshee's Wail, you deal an additional 1d12 Necrotic damage.

**Tears of Venus**
On his 3rd visit the General requested of the Artificer a way to control the battlefield more effectively, to rain down the Nine Hells upon his enemies. The artificer went to work immediately, studying weather, consulting with notable meteorologists, and reading through his collection of fiendish tomes to create this hellish rain machine. The resulting weapon’s metals all have a sickly greenish hue to them and gold banding decorates the muzzle.

The 2.5ft mortar tube is easily loaded, taking only a bonus action to load. As an action you may fire the Acid Shell 100 feet into the sky where, on initiative 20 in the next round, it will burst and begin to rain Acid droplets down in a 30 foot diameter. Creatures that start their turns in the area affected make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. They take 3d4 acid damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The rain lasts for 1 round.

Acid Shells can be made with Alchemist’s tools and cost 3 vials of acid

**Bolt Thrower**
Firearm (chaingun) 
Ammunition (range 50/150), burst fire only, heavy, two-handed

By this point the General had been raised up to having control over most of the surrounding lands. He approached the artificer with gleam of arrogance and commanded he be made a weapon that the Gods themselves would kneel to and truly show his dominion over all. As always the Artificer went right to work, a gleam in his eye.

A large platinum multi barreled gun attached to a  hefty ammo pack, slung over shoulders with thick metal chains, was the result of his work. The barrels crackle with electricity as the gun spins up. While attuned to this you have resistance lightning damage.

*Spin Up*
Before you make a burst attack with the chaingun, it must spin up. This takes a bonus action. Once the chaingun is spinning, it remains spinning until the end of your next turn in which you do not attack with it.

*Lightning Shackles* 
Bolts of lightning spray from the barrels as you pull the trigger on the spun up gun. You choose up to 5 targets that are all within at least 15 feet of one of the other targets. They must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 4d8 Lightning damage and are restrained as the electric current surges through their body’s, or half as much and suffer no other ill effects on a success.

*Static Burst*
As a reaction to getting hit by an attack and as long as the chaingun is spun up, you can make all creatures within 5ft of you make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. Taking 2d8 lightning damage and disadvantage on the next attack they make on a failure or half as much and no disadvantage on a success. After using this you need to Spin Up again.

**Finger Guns**
Wondrous item

Many seasons had passed since the General last went to the Artificer. He was an old withered conqueror now and sought something to help his grandchildren grow into better men than he was, while still allowing him to be playful with them. The Artificer said they had just the thing and gave the General the finger guns. And with that gesture the General fell dead before the Artificer.

The Finger Guns are a pair of bracelets that when both are worn you gain the ability to shoot psychic energy at creatures with just a “finger gun” of your fingers. They have a number of charges equal to your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1) and recharge at dawn. You can spend one of the charges as an action in the following ways:

*Champ:*
With confidence in your friends and sincerity in your voice you lift up those around you with your finger guns. You choose a friendly creature within 30 feet of you and give them 1d10 inspiration for their next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.

*Chump:*
With disdain in your foes and sarcasm in your speech, you tear down your enemies with insincere comments. You choose a creature within 30 feet of you to make a DC 15 Intelligence saving throw. They take 2d6 psychic damage and can’t take reactions until the end of it’s next turn on a failure or half as much on a success and suffer none of the other ill effects.

**Whisper Powder**
*Wondrous item (consumable)*

A shimmering fae powder that when sprinkled on a creature affects only them with the silence spell. While affected this way you have advantage on stealth checks to not be heard. The effect lasts for 10 minutes.

**Penny’s Peerless Power Polishes**
*Wondrous item (consumable)*

A brand of black market nail polish often used to smuggle magic into places where it aught not belong. Mixed with a dash of negator shroom spores to block magic detection from spells and abilities that would do so. Currently on the market there are only six colors each with their own effect:

*Revolutionary Red:*Your fierce passion for the cause explodes out with this polish. You can cast  Fireball(3rd level, DC 14).

*Cat’s Paw Purple:* Display how safe and innocent you are with a simple flourish of your hand, before striking your foe. You can cast Hypnotic Pattern(3rd level, DC14).

*Bear-garden Black:* Interrupt those that would try to cast down on you with a raucous interjection. You can cast Counterspell(3rd level, only affects spells of 3rd level or lower).

*Ben’s Brilliant Blue:* Be as smart, striking, and fashionable as the big brain himself, Benjamin Franklin. Strike a pose and you can cast Lightning Bolt(3rd level, DC14).

*Gilly-Gaupus Green:* Some consider this green to be a bit silly, prove them wrong and show them they are true Gillyguapus. You can cast Bestow Curse(3rd level, DC14, no concentration).

*Proletarian Pink:* Penny’s personal polish, practical, pure, and a protector of proletarian. Stand before you fellows and lead them to rise up. You can cast Motivational Speech(3rd level).

You can only cast these spells once per application and only one color may be applied at a time. Each bottle has 5 applications.

**Sentinel Stuffy** 
*Wondrous item (requires attunement)*

A plush toy that more often than not finds the new owner, before the owner finds it. This doll attunes itself to you upon being picked up. While attuned to it and on your person, you gain a +1 to your AC and all saving throws. The stuffy acts as an Unseen Servant with the following changes, it has an AC of 13, 10 hit points, and a Strength of 10.The Sentinel Stuffy also has minimal sentience with an Intelligence of 4(-3), Wisdom of 10(+0), and a Charisma of 16(+3) It cannot speak, but understands all languages spoken by its owner. If you are separated from the Sentinel Stuffy for over 24hrs you will lose attunement, during this time the Stuffy will do all it can to get back to you.If you were to die due to overwhelming damage or from failing death saves, the Sentinel Stuffy takes your place when dying.

**Odd Heart**
*Wondrous item (requires attunement)*

This item is one that has always been with you, your own heart, and its potential only unlocked by an experimental surgery. If you manage to survive the surgery you will awaken to your heart being encapsulated in a containment chamber of your own choosing and connected by a tubing or a cord to your chest. After the surgery you will find yourself permanently under the effect of Sanctuary(DC15) until you are unattuned. Whenever you roll hit die you always take maximum healing. Once attuned to the Odd Heart you cannot unattune to it unless you die or undergo a more dangerous reversal surgery.

*Symbiotic Nature.*
The heart can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your attunement to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse or enter an anti-magic zone, your attunement to the heart ends, and you immediately fall unconscious and start making death saves.

**Phlogiston Pigdin**
*Wondrous item (requires attunement) *

This prosthetic tongue was made with magi whom have had their tongues forcibly removed. Taking a lump of molten phlogiston and molding it carefully, a person could replace their lost tongue. 

The extra dimensional energies inherent in the Phlogiston imbue the attuned with the languages of all the planes. While attuned you can cast *Tongues* on yourself a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus rounded down and resets on a long rest. You can also cast *Speak with Animals, Plants, and Dead* at will. 

You also gain proficiency in one of the following abilities: Deception, Intimidation, or Persuasion. If you are already proficient in the chosen ability you gain expertise instead.

If exposed to an anti-magic zone or other similar effects, the Phlogiston Pigdin detaches from you and you become unattuned.
